astranl.do_not_use_when: you only have a generic description without a part number (use ask_astranl), or you need a binding quote or delivery date
astranl.example_intent: Mitsubishi says Q03UDCPU ends production; is any still in stock and what is the successor?
astranl.next_possible_action: verify_astranl with the astralock_event id; check_counterparty_nl before paying a seller; create_task when a physical step is needed in the Netherlands
astranl.proof_level: seller-reported structured data at observation time, digest sealed by AstraNL; not a quote
astranl.returns: summary with availability, stock, sellers, authorized sellers, lowest EUR price seen, lifecycle; manufacturer_lifecycle with status, date, named successor and page sha256 where held; exact offers; per-source status; sanctions screening; proof with digest, moment seal and AstraLock event
astranl.use_when: you need to know whether a specific machine, robot, PLC, drive, servo, gearbox, sensor or electronic part is really obtainable now, from whom, at roughly what price, with proof

annotations.title: Ground a component in live market reality

description: Ground a machine, robot or industrial automation component in live market reality with ONE call. Give a manufacturer part number and optionally the maker. AstraNL queries its verified distributor connections (Nexar/Octopart, Mouser, element14/Farnell NL, OEMsecrets) in parallel, keeps only offers whose part number matches exactly after normalisation, screens maker and sellers against the EU consolidated sanctions list and the US Consolidated Screening List, and returns availability, stock seen, authorized sellers, lowest unit price seen in EUR, lifecycle values and per-source status. When AstraNL holds the manufacturer own lifecycle or discontinuation page for the part, the answer also carries manufacturer_lifecycle: status, date, the successor the manufacturer names and the page SHA-256, kept separate from seller-reported values; asking for a successor also shows which discontinued part it replaces. Every fresh answer carries a SHA-256 digest sealed with the AstraNL moment seal and an AstraLock event id you can check later with verify_astranl. Limits: distributor data is seller-reported at the observed time, not a quote and not a delivery promise; NOT_FOUND_IN_CHECKED_SOURCES means only these sources; answers are cached for 24 hours. Never orders, contacts or pays anyone. Writes (why the tool is not read-only): each fresh answer, not one served from the 24 hour cache, appends one event to the public AstraLock log with the part number, the maker, the digest, the availability and the number of exact offers, so the answer can be verified later, and stores the answer in an AstraNL database table (component_groundings) that serves the cache and counts the budget; the row names only the door (mcp), nothing about the caller. Live budget: 40 fresh reads a day across all MCP callers; after that only cached answers, status DAILY_LIVE_BUDGET_SPENT. Logging: every MCP call is journaled with the tool name, outcome, argument length, caller class (external, probe, crawler, self), a SHA-256 hash of the caller network /24 and the client family; for demand statistics also the first 160 characters of a query, question, title or id argument and the user-agent; never the address itself, other arguments or an account.

manufacturer.description: optional maker name, e.g. Allen-Bradley; offers from other makers are then dropped

mpn.description: manufacturer part number, exactly as printed by the maker, e.g. 1756-L85E
